lessonTitle: Difference Between Informing, Persuading, Exploring and Co-Creating

slides.title: Every Conversation Falls Into One Mode
bullets: All four modes exist whether an MSL chooses deliberately or by default
Telling them apart precisely is a core compliance and effectiveness skill
Only two of the four belong in routine scientific exchange

slides.title: Informing Is Necessary but One-Directional
bullets: Accurately and completely communicating study results, mechanism, safety data and guidelines
Must include limitations and unfavourable findings, not just favourable ones
Legitimate on its own, but used exclusively it is a presentation, not a dialogue

slides.title: Persuading Crosses the Firewall
bullets: Goal is changing behaviour toward a commercial outcome
Belongs to Commercial and promotional communication, not Medical Affairs
Even subtle, selectively emphasised persuasion breaks the Medical-Commercial firewall

slides.title: Exploring Is Where Insight Lives
bullets: Genuine questions about clinical experience, concerns and unmet needs
Real openness to what the answer might be, not a lead-in to a predetermined response
The mode most under-used by MSLs more comfortable presenting data

slides.title: Co-Creating Has a Narrow Home
bullets: Jointly developing a research question or hypothesis with the expert
Appropriate for advisory boards, investigator studies and publication planning
Not a default for routine field visits — trust and governance requirements are not met

slides.title: Name the Mode You Are Actually In
bullets: Before and during any interaction, an MSL should be able to name which mode is active
Correct course immediately if the conversation drifts toward persuading

takeaway.title: Naming which of the four modes a conversation is in is what keeps scientific exchange genuine
bullets: Informing and exploring are the two legitimate modes of routine exchange
Persuading and unstructured co-creating are compliance risks, not conversational style
Self-awareness in the moment is what prevents drift
